source.title: Sycophancy Suppression Can Impair Rational Updating: Anti-Sycophancy Should Preserve the Ability to Update
source.authors: Huanhuan Ma; Henry Peng Zou; Cheng-Ze Li; En-Ze Ma; Yunan Su; Philip S. Yu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses cross-patching, rather than an attribution-graph reconstruction test, to evaluate whether attributed MLP components causally recover behavior-related metric changes. This bears conceptually on V5, but does not test its full claim.
record.gate_note: The study does not audit neuron poles or measure the share with one or two jobs, explanation quality on held-out activating examples, or automated explanation scores. Its other behavioral intervention results concern unsupported-yielding and rational-updating, not the neuron claims in the remaining versions. The cross-patching result and random controls are retained because they test the functional contribution of attributed MLP components.
record.test_reason: This is a sycophancy study. It uses gradient attribution patching over MLP neurons and heads in 3B–8B models as a tool to locate components, then cross-patches them only to check that tool (§5.3–5.4: it 'supports using the attributed components for the overlap analysis'). It builds no attribution graph, makes no claim that neurons explain behaviour without a replacement model, and reports no reconstruction error. The models are not large. No neuron-pole audit, explanation scoring or vision work bears on V1–V4, V6 or V7. The cross-patch recovery is a validation of the study's own method, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right but misses the main point. The authors conclude that anti-sycophancy is a selectivity problem: DPO, SFT and steering interventions that reduce unsupported yielding often impair rational updating, even under joint training. They explain this by overlapping attributed MLP neurons and heads and positively aligned steering directions. Orthogonalized steering gives only modest, backbone-dependent gains. Cross-patching is presented as a validation of their attribution, not as a claim about neurons as explanatory units.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-based component attribution and cross-patching rather than testing attribution graphs against a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-patching recovery varies across models and k in Figure 3; the text gives an aggregate 63–85% range at k=5000.

fits_no_version.finding: In four 3B–8B instruction-tuned models on PopQA, cross-patching the top-5000 attributed MLP components from pressure/evidence runs into baseline runs recovers 63–85% of the prompt-induced logit-margin shift. Layer-matched and uniform random sets of the same size recover close to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of gradient-attributed MLP neurons in mid-size LLMs causally carries most of a behaviour-specific logit shift (sycophantic yielding / evidence updating), far above random neuron sets.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The cross-patching recovery is reported as an aggregate range across four relatively small instruction-tuned models and is evaluated on PopQA. It measures recovery of a prompt-induced metric shift, not complete behavioral reconstruction or explanation quality on held-out examples.
record.rows_left_out: No other result was omitted for V5. Behavioral intervention metrics, component-overlap rates, and steering-direction cosines were not extracted as rows because they do not measure the attribution-graph explanation or reconstruction claim in V5.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or one-job/two-job/unexplained shares.
No interpretability-share audit across models, MoE or scale.
No vision neurons, no cat-and-car example, no recursive generalization.
No architecture/tool comparison and no interpretable-neuron estimates.
Not tested. There are no neuron attribution graphs explaining behaviour, no large model, no replacement-model comparison and no reconstruction error.
No neuron explanations from activating examples.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels (supports / limits_scope on V5) are removed. The record's own tranche_reason concedes the study does not test V5's claim, and the cross-patch result is a method sanity check (a T4 use). The study also notes that sparse-feature circuits might separate the behaviours more cleanly. That is a remark, not a result bearing on V5.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B pole-level audit or estimates of one-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No audit of interpretability shares across model scales, dense versus MoE architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose interpretation, or recursive-generalization analysis.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, tools, or interpretable-neuron estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.

Tests functional recovery from cross-patching attributed MLP components, not attribution graphs as a whole; does not test large-model scale, compare against a trained replacement model, or report reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations written from activating examples predict firing on separate examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-3-4B, and Qwen3-8B (aggregate reported range)
rows.operation_detail: Cross-patched top-k attributed MLP components from pressure or evidence runs into baseline runs; reported recovery of the prompt-induced metric shift.
rows.measure: Fraction of prompt-induced metric shift recovered by the top-k attributed components
rows.baseline: BASELINE run without feedback; recovery is measured against the prompt-induced shift
rows.uncertainty: Figure bands are ±1 std over 3 seeds; specific standard deviations not stated.
rows.note: The text reports an aggregate range across the four backbones, rather than per-model values. Components are MLP components; this is not a full attribution-graph reconstruction test.
rows.check: Validation of the study's own attribution method, not a test of V5. Recovery of a single logit-margin shift on PopQA by top-k MLP units is not an attribution graph explaining behaviour. It has no replacement-model comparison and no reconstruction error, and the models are small (3B–8B). The 63–85% is an aggregate range at k=5000 read from text; per-model values appear only in Figure 3.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Top-k attributed MLP components, PopQA cross-patching, k=5000
reader_labels.reason: Attributed components recover 63–85% of the prompt-induced metric shift, while both random controls stay close to zero; this supports functional relevance of the components in this setting (r1–r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PopQA cross-patching and the tested component sets
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is partial, and the study does not test attribution-graph reconstruction, replacement-model comparisons, or reconstruction error (r1).
